stimulus.source_note: Jan Collaert I after Jan van der Straet (Stradanus), 'The Invention of Sugar Refinery', Nova Reperta plate 13, c. 1600, Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain (CC0).
stimulus.text: The engraving shows a sugar refinery in the Americas around 1600. In the background, workers cut sugarcane in the fields. Inside, workers crush the cane, boil the juice in large vats over fires, and pour the syrup into cone-shaped molds to form sugar loaves. The work is done by hand, in stages, by many workers at once.

stem: The engraving shows the stages of sugar making: cutting cane, crushing it, boiling the juice, and molding sugar loaves. What does this sequence best show about sugar production in the Americas?

options.text: Sugar was made only by machines, with no human labor at all.
options.misconception: The work in the image is done by hand; machines came much later.

options.text: Sugar was made by hand in stages, needing many workers at once.
Sugar grew wild and needed no workers to harvest or refine it.
options.misconception: The image shows workers cutting, crushing, and boiling; sugar needed much labor.

options.text: Sugar was refined in Europe and shipped finished to the Americas.
options.misconception: The refinery in the image stands in the Americas, where the cane grew.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
